claims.claim_text: Bloom Energy has deployed approximately 1.2 gigawatts (cumulative) of Energy Servers accepted across more than 1,200 locations and 7 countries, with 1,241 MW net accepted as of year-end 2023 (up 268 MW from 973 MW).
claims.source_quote: With approximately 1.2 gigawatts of the Energy Servers accepted in more than 1,200 locations and 7 countries, our platform empowers ... The increase in acceptances of 268 megawatts achieved for the year ended December 31, 2023 was added to our installed base and, therefore, increased our total megawatts accepted, net, from 973 megawatts to 1,241 megawatts.
claims.subject: Bloom Energy Corp.

proposed_connector.name: eia_form860.query_generator_capacity
proposed_connector.description: EIA Form 860 annual generator-level survey — every operating electric generator in the US with nameplate capacity >=1 MW reports owner, technology (fuel cells under 'FC'), nameplate MW, in-service date, state, and county. Authoritative US generator registry for behind-the-meter and grid-tied fuel cells.
proposed_connector.sample_invocation: Download eia8602023.zip; parse 3_1_Generator_Y2023.xlsx and filter where TECHNOLOGY contains 'Fuel Cell' and OWNER_NAME or PLANT_NAME contains 'Bloom'.
proposed_connector.rationale: Bloom's 1.2 GW cumulative-accepted figure is a registry-verifiable installed-capacity claim. EIA Form 860 captures every >=1 MW fuel-cell generator in the US (large fraction of Bloom's installed base) with owner, technology, and in-service date — adjudicates the 1.2 GW headline against the US generator registry. Absence of corroborating MW totals weakens the deployment claim.
proposed_connector.completeness: All US electric generators >=1 MW; misses sub-MW and many international/Korean installations.

claims.extraction_notes: Most distinctive Bloom claim and headline planned-vs-operational test (Calibration Heuristic 3). EIA-860 is the canonical US fuel-cell-generator registry. edgar_fts cannot count MW; NHTSA/NREL irrelevant. Capacity-in-operation per EIA vs. company's 'accepted' figure is the critical adjudication.

claims.claim_text: Bloom's primary manufacturing facilities for Energy Servers and Electrolyzer assembly are in Fremont, California (multi-gigawatt factory) and Newark, Delaware (178,000 sq ft, the first purpose-built Bloom manufacturing center).
claims.source_quote: Our primary manufacturing facilities for Energy Servers and Electrolyzers assembly are in Fremont, California, and Newark, Delaware ... our 178,000 square-foot manufacturing facility in Newark, which was our first purpose-built Bloom Energy manufacturing center ... In 2023, we scaled up production at our multi-gigawatt factory in Fremont, California
claims.subject: Bloom Energy Corp.
claims.extraction_notes: Solid oxide fuel cell manufacturing involves ceramic/electrolyte processing and is industrial; should register in EPA FRS. Newark DE is the most material US factory (purpose-built, 178,000 sq ft, with electrolyzer line being added). Absence in FRS would weaken the multi-GW-factory claim. Fremont CA can be checked separately.

claims.claim_text: SK ecoplant, Bloom's primary distributor in the Republic of Korea, committed in October 2021 to purchase at least 500 MW of Energy Servers between 2022 and 2024 on a take-or-pay basis, and on December 21, 2023 expanded the partnership with an incremental purchase commitment of 250 MW through 2027.
claims.source_quote: In October 2021, we announced an expansion of our existing partnership with SK ecoplant, which included purchase commitments of at least 500 megawatts of power for our Energy Servers between 2022 and 2024 on a take-or-pay basis, the creation of hydrogen innovation centers ... On December 21, 2023, we expanded our partnership with SK ecoplant through an incremental purchase commitment of 250 megawatts through 2027
claims.subject: SK ecoplant Co., Ltd.

proposed_connector.name: dart_fss.query_counterparty_disclosure
proposed_connector.description: Korea Financial Supervisory Service DART (Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer) system — full-text and form search across all Korean public-company filings. SK ecoplant filed an aborted KOSPI IPO prospectus and SK Inc. (parent) files quarterly disclosures referencing material subsidiaries. DART is the Korean counterpart to EDGAR.
proposed_connector.rationale: SK ecoplant is a privately-held Korean entity (failed KOSPI IPO) so its commitments do not appear in EDGAR. Layer 3 Rule 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold) requires the counterparty to corroborate a 500 MW take-or-pay commitment — for SK ecoplant that means DART filings (either its own or its listed parent SK Inc., ticker 034730.KS). Absence of any DART reference to Bloom while Bloom counts SK ecoplant as a ~37% customer is a HARD CONTRADICTION.
proposed_connector.completeness: All Korean public-company disclosures; private-co coverage via material-subsidiary references in parent filings.

claims.extraction_notes: SK ecoplant is the single most material counterparty (likely the 37% customer per the concentration disclosure). Cannot use edgar_fts because counterparty is not SEC-registered. DART is the authoritative Korean equivalent. Also note: SK ecoplant's parent SK Inc. is listed on KOSPI; its annual report should reference material Bloom commitments under Korean K-IFRS related-party / commitment disclosure rules.

claims.claim_text: In the year ended December 31, 2023, two customers accounted for approximately 37% and 26% of Bloom's total revenue (a combined 63% from two customers).
claims.source_quote: During the year ended December 31, 2023, revenue from two customers accounted for approximately 37% and 26% of our total revenue, respectively. ... in the year ended December 31, 2023, two customers accounted for approximately 37% and 26% of our total revenue. The loss of any large customer order or any delays in installations of new products with any large customer would materially and adversely affect our business results.
claims.subject: Bloom Energy Corp.
claims.extraction_notes: Verifies that Bloom's own filings repeatedly disclose the concentration pattern and lets us cross-check by looking at filings where Bloom is named (counterparty corroboration). The 37% customer is almost certainly SK ecoplant (Korean distributor) given the size; the 26% customer is more diagnostic — likely a US Managed Services financier or a major direct customer. edgar_fts adjudicates by counting filings (mainly 8-Ks under Item 1.01 for material contracts) that reference Bloom by name from non-Bloom CIKs. NOTE: deep counterparty-corroboration ideally would query individual customer CIKs once identified, which Phase-2 may infer from 8-K material contract filings.

claims.claim_text: Bloom holds 325 active US patents and 145 active international patents as of December 31, 2023, plus 414 patent applications pending.
claims.source_quote: As of December 31, 2023, we have 325 active patents in the U.S. and 145 active patents internationally. ... active patents and 414 patent applications pending. Our U.S. patents are expected to expire between 2022 and 2042.
claims.subject: Bloom Energy Corp.
claims.object_value: 325 US + 145 international active patents; 414 pending applications
claims.extraction_notes: USPTO ODP adjudicates the 325 active US patents and lets us bucket them by fuel-cell vs. electrolyzer to test the claim that Bloom is leveraging the same SOFC platform across products. A materially smaller granted-patent count, or near-zero electrolyzer-specific patents, weakens the electrolyzer technology-platform claim. Cross-check with Plansee/GTP arbitration (separate claim) — patents 8,802,328, 8,753,785, 9,434,003 disputed.

claims.claim_text: Bloom is in active arbitration with former supplier Plansee SE / Global Tungsten & Powders Corp. (Plansee/GTP) over inventorship and infringement of U.S. Patents 8,802,328, 8,753,785, and 9,434,003, with the arbitrator on October 2, 2023 ruling all claims arbitrable and bifurcating into phases through 2024-2025.
claims.source_quote: In February 2022, Plansee SE/Global Tungsten & Powders Corp. ( Plansee/GTP ), a former supplier, filed a request for expedited arbitration with the World Intellectual Property Organization Arbitration and Mediation Center in Geneva Switzerland ( WIPO ), for various claims allegedly in relation to an Intellectual Property and Confidential Disclosure Agreement ... Plansee/GTP s statement of claims includes allegations of infringement of U.S. Patent Nos. 8,802,328, 8,753,785 and 9,434,003 ... On October 2, 2023, the arbitrator in the WIPO proceeding issued a ruling concluding that all the parties claims were arbitrable.
claims.subject: Bloom Energy Corp.
claims.object_value: Plansee SE / Global Tungsten & Powders (WIPO; US Patents 8,802,328 / 8,753,785 / 9,434,003)
claims.extraction_notes: USPTO ODP adjudicates the inventorship side of the three patents-in-suit by listing their actual assignee (Plansee/GTP vs. Bloom). If Plansee/GTP is the registered assignee, the inventorship-correction claim Bloom is pursuing is non-trivial and indicates real exposure to a counterclaim/loss-of-IP risk. Eastern District of Texas / WIPO proceeding cadence is also visible via edgar_fts on Bloom's own filings as an ancillary check.

claims.claim_text: Bloom's Energy Servers and Electrolyzer are eligible for IRA Section 48 ITC and Section 45V Clean Hydrogen PTC (up to $3/kg for 10 years), and Bloom has applied for a Section 48C Qualified Advanced Energy Project credit for expanding manufacturing capacity.
claims.source_quote: Section 48 the ITC, which provides a tax credit based on capital investment in a variety of renewable and conventional energy technologies ... Section 48C Qualified Advanced Energy Project (reenacted), which provides an ITC through a competitive application process administered through the Department of Energy ... Section 45V Clean Hydrogen, which provides a PTC of up to $3 per kg of qualified clean hydrogen ... the IRA authorized a competitive process to apply for credits to expand or enhance manufacturing capacity under IRC 48C, and we have applied for a credit under this provision; at this time, we cannot be assured our application will ultimately be accepted
claims.subject: Bloom Energy Corp.
claims.object_value: IRC Section 48C (DOE-administered Qualified Advanced Energy Project)

proposed_connector.name: doe_48c.query_qualified_advanced_energy_project_awards
proposed_connector.description: DOE Office of Manufacturing & Energy Supply Chains (MESC) Section 48C Qualified Advanced Energy Project Tax Credit allocation listings. DOE publishes named recipient lists and credit amounts for each 48C round on energy.gov; first round awarded March 29, 2024.
proposed_connector.sample_invocation: Fetch the DOE 48C Round 1 award announcement PDF/HTML and grep recipient list for 'Bloom Energy'; cross-check Treasury/IRS Notice 2024-26 appendix of awardees.
proposed_connector.rationale: Bloom's IRA 48C application is a binary verifiable fact: either DOE awarded a 48C credit to Bloom or it did not. By cutoff 2024-05-17, DOE Round 1 results were public (announced 2024-03-29). DOE/Treasury award lists are the only authoritative adjudicator — no SEC filing required because the awardee list is public.
proposed_connector.completeness: All 48C award rounds publicly announced by DOE/Treasury.

claims.extraction_notes: Bloom's IRA narrative is foundational to its hydrogen/electrolyzer thesis. 48C awardee status is binary and pre-cutoff verifiable (Round 1 March 2024). usaspending does NOT index 48C credits (they are tax-side, not contract/grant); DOE press list is the authoritative source. PROPOSED rather than usaspending.

claims.claim_text: Bloom deployed the world's largest solid oxide electrolyzer at NASA Ames Research Center in Mountain View, California, achieving 37.5 kWh of electricity per kilogram of hydrogen — described by Idaho National Laboratory as the most efficient electrolyzer INL had tested in 2023.
claims.source_quote: we deployed the world s largest solid oxide electrolyzer at our NASA Ames Research Center, located in Mountain View, California, and achieved a new record electrical efficiency level of 37.5 kWh of electricity per kilogram of hydrogen generated. ... The Idaho National Laboratory (INL) has been studying to see how well it could produce hydrogen from electricity and steam from a nuclear facility, and their 2023 results showed that it was the most efficient electrolyzer that they ever tested.
claims.subject: Bloom Energy Corp.
claims.object_value: NASA Ames Research Center, Mountain View, CA; INL-tested
claims.extraction_notes: If NASA Ames is hosting a Bloom electrolyzer demo, there should be a NASA or DOE contract / cooperative agreement to Bloom (or the inverse — Bloom paid NASA for use of the site). usaspending captures DOE / NASA federal awards to Bloom. Absence of any federal award narrows the claim to a marketing-only deployment vs. a federally-corroborated demonstration project. INL test result is separately corroborated by INL publications but unverifiable via the catalog connectors.
